Unlike the baseline hierarchical pruning which preserves the full tree structure within active regions, far-field culling aggressively simplifies the geometry representation in empty space, improving tracing performance by up to a factor of 2 on complex scenes [S1].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that 'far-field culling replaces entire sub trees with constants that remain valid lower distance bounds further away from the object' (Section 6.1) and that this technique 'improves the tracing performance by up to a factor of 2' on specific complex scenes (City, Gameboy, Camera) compared to the baseline (Section 3.6 and Section 6). The claim accurately reflects these findings regarding the mechanism (simplifying geometry in empty space/far-field) and the performance improvement.
